pr_body:
In the past, the `this` of every hook was the same as the context where it has been registered, while the `this` of the route-specific hooks is the same as the plugin where the route is registered. This could lead to some confusion, as the `this` changes during time, while it's better to have it consistent.

This pr addresses this issue, take a look at the test to see the new behavior.
This should not break current application code, but it's safer to release it in a server major change.

Closes: https://github.com/fastify/fastify/issues/1587

issue_context.title: Enable to set all hooks (including .use middlewares) in route()
issue_context.body:
## 🚀 Feature Proposal

Currently we do not expose an API to add `onRequest` and route specific middlewares, however our codebase can definitely support them. Adding them would ensure an higher level of flexibility combined with the new `onRoute`  hook.

Missing things:

* [x] `onRequest` - done in https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/1594
* [ ] `onSend`
* [ ] `onError`
* [x] `onResponse`
* [ ] middlewares

## Example

Please provide an example for how this feature would be used.

```js
app.route({
  method: 'GET',
  async onRoute (req, reply) { },
  middlewares: [function (req, res, next) {
    next()
  }]
}, async (req, reply) => {})
```
comments: Would they be called middlewares? That’s a term we use to reference Express modules that we support.
Do they get invoked before the handler? Are they before the `preHandler` or after?
Sounds like a good idea to me 👍

https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/2005 will fix this one thanks to the for loop that we will use behind the scenes.
It will not apply for middlewares tho.

review_comments: Can you move this logic into the `hooks.js` file?  It seems way more useful to share this, also because it's duplicated in `route.js`.

Not sure what you mean, for having this working we need to work with this closure.
Moving to an external file will only make the core a little more complicated for saving 6 lines. Furthermore, now with the for loop and the `lifecycleHooks` array the code is more future proof, as if we will add new hooks, this code will continue to work as expected and handle the new hook as well.
